newsitem.title: CHINA: China endorses Hong Kong's leader-elect.
newsitem.headline: China endorses Hong Kong's leader-elect.

text.p: China formally endorsed Hong Kong's newly anointed leader-in-waiting, Tung Chee-hwa, on Thursday, recognising his landslide victory.

The 59-year-old shipping magnate proved the overwhelming choice of a Beijing-vetted panel on Wednesday that voted him the man to lead the territory after its transition from British to Chinese rule next year.

China's Preparatory Committee, the 150-strong body of prominent Hong Kong and Chinese citizens set up to manage the handover, extended China's recognition of Tung's new role at a session in the southern boomtown of Shenzhen.
The endorsement was proposed by Preparatory Committee vice-chairman Wang Hanbin.
"If you don't have any objection, then approve it by applauding," Wang said.
The delegates, who include some of Hong Kong's wealthiest and most powerful tycoons and deal-makers, dutifully clapped in unison.
Tung, whose father fled the Chinese communist revolution in 1949, will take over the helm when Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30, ending more than 150 years as a British colony.
His victory was considered a foregone conclusion in Hong Kong.
